title: Bishop and knight against a lone king: the right corner
outcomes: States the two phases and the textbook corner rule
Finds the first move of a bishop-and-knight mate with the king already near the right corner
Tells a mating position from a look-alike with the bishop on the wrong colour, and a win from a fifty-move draw

steps.text: **Bishop and knight** can mate a bare king, but by the textbook rule only around a corner of the **bishop's colour**: with a light-squared bishop, h1 or a8. There are two phases. The king, bishop and knight first push the lone king to an edge, then drive it along the edge to the right corner. Here the king already stands beside h1; the mate comes on g1.

steps.caption: White to move mates in five. Black's king is on the h-file; the white bishop stands on a light square, like the corner h1.

line.say: A quiet bishop move. There is no check.
Black's king goes into the corner h1.
White's king comes to g3, next to the corner area.
Black's king steps to g1, still on the edge.
The knight comes towards the action.
Black's king goes back to h1.
Check from the bishop on g2; the white king on g3 guards that square.
Checkmate: the knight attacks g1, and the bishop and king cover the other squares.

claims.statement: Bh3 starts a forced mate in five.
The tablebase result for White is a win.

steps.caption: The final net. Bishop g2, king g3 and knight e2 against a king on g1: the bishop covers f1 and h1, the king covers f2 and h2, and the knight gives the check. The bishop's colour, the corner and the clock decide whether you can reach such a net.

steps.text: **Two conditions.** The corner must match the bishop; if the king sits in the wrong corner you must drive it out and along the edge to the other one. And the fifty-move count keeps running: a win can still be a draw if too few moves are left. Predict each look-alike.

steps.title: Right bishop colour or wrong
steps.prompt: White to move. In the first position the bishop's colour matches the corner h1. Predict whether a mate in two exists; then see the bishop on a dark square, and the knight on the other wing.

steps.title: The same win with the clock running
steps.prompt: Same pieces and squares each time; only the halfmove clock differs, and each prompt states it. The first position is a win. Predict the other two.
Before each move: did you check the colour of your bishop and the corner you were driving towards? What did you forget?
